rationale: Low-protein Parkinson diets measured daily OFF time without an isolated roasted-potato arm. The N-DOSE protocol includes a broad potato or vegetable diet example and an OFF-time item with no linked result. A case-control questionnaire pools fried and roasted potatoes. The preparation-specific daily OFF comparison remains unresolved.

A cooked-onion allergy case recorded acute dysphonia. The heated peel-extract trial uses about 1,000 mg active extract in 1,200 mg of capsules and reports a respiratory hoarseness item with baseline imbalance. Listener-rated speech after cooked onion in Parkinson disease remains unmeasured.

An earlier sustained-attention comparison with dried pepper was inconclusive. The Alzheimer formulation reports reduced impaired concentration within the active group, using black pepper with Bunium persicum. Item-level contrast and isolated cracked-pepper exposure remain unverified. The Parkinson attention comparison remains open.

Oregano animal experiments use extracts, several routes and behavior proxies. A new human forehead-oil study measured depression in an uncontrolled series. A separate inhaled marjoram trial gives inconclusive between-arm anxiety comparisons. A dried oregano and Parkinson anxiety comparison remains open.

Human sleep trials use corn oil as a common vehicle or comparison and do not isolate its effect. SHAPE reports conflict on the oil label, and its original dissertation identifies soybean oil. Registered sleep outcomes and exact original military tables remain open. The refined-corn-oil Parkinson insomnia comparison remains unresolved.
